entries.title: Draw This, Then Die!

review.en:
Episode #10: 90% of Everything Is Crap ~ I Need Friends to Become Stronger Than Mama

"Honestly, the score may be a little generous, but there's no question that Akafuku-chan's greatness was on full display—a perfect 10 out of 10."

This might be giving it a little extra credit, but after ten episodes where Akafuku-chan had barely had any obvious standout moments—or really given me much reason to see her value—this episode finally showed us what she's truly capable of. And she came through hard. That was so good. I also loved the contrast between Teshima's feelings about the past and what it was actually like when she finally came face-to-face with Hebiichigo. Just two episodes left... Where is this going?
review.jp:
第10話: この世の90%はカスである~ママより強くなるには『友達』が必要である

"正直緩めの評価だが、赤福ちゃんの素晴らしさが10点満点で表されていたのは間違いない"

『ちょっとオマケかも知れないけど、これまでの10話でほとんどこれと言ったわかりやすい見せ場、価値をそこまで感じられなかった赤福ちゃんの真髄が出ていた。それもかなりツヨい。良かったなぁ。そして手島の過去の思いと実際のヘビイチゴとの対面のギャップも良かった。後2話・・・どうなる?』

entries.title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Season 4
entries.jpTitle: 『Re:ゼロから始める異世界生活』4th season（奪還編）

review.en:
Episode #5: Subaru Natsuki

"The idea of these different selves, each shaped by a different set of memories and a different point in time, eventually coming back together into the original Subaru—while all of them were still 'him' in the end—was fascinating. A very generous bonus."

Season 4 has been like this all along, but I still feel there are just too many scenes and developments designed to tug at your heartstrings—to make you cry or otherwise hit you with some big emotional moment. This time, though, I thought the whole process of having Subaru's memories eaten, gradually recovering them, and ultimately becoming "Natsuki Subaru" again—the person built from all of those memories and experiences—was portrayed wonderfully.

What made it especially interesting was how the Subarus from different points in his journey, each carrying the memories and experiences of that particular point in time, could come to feel almost like separate people. To the current Subaru, who had lost everything that came before, the Subaru he used to be had become this extraordinary figure almost separate from himself—someone far greater than he believed himself capable of being. And as he recovered his memories and encountered those different past selves one by one, each of them could likewise feel distinct from the others. Yet those past Subarus had struggled too. They had doubted themselves, hated their own weakness, and felt that they weren't nearly as strong or remarkable as they now appeared from the perspective of the Subaru looking back at them. In the end, each of those selves was different, and yet each was still Natsuki Subaru—and so was the Subaru standing there now. Seeing all of those seemingly separate selves ultimately reconnect and become one again was incredibly well done.

That is precisely why I found it so effective to see his feelings toward those other selves—including his original self—gradually change as he recovered everything, until he was finally able to reconnect with the person he had been all along. I found myself thinking, "That's clever... and actually a really interesting way of looking at it." Each version of him exists separately at its own point in time, yet there must also be something consistent running through all of them, and perhaps the things they feel and the things that truly matter to them don't really change. Even with ourselves, who we were at another point in our lives might look completely different when viewed from where we are now—perhaps almost like another person altogether—but that doesn't change the fact that it was still us. We change and grow, but we rarely get to truly confront those past versions of ourselves. I thought this was a fascinating way of giving form to that idea, and I really liked that this was what the episode chose to focus on.

That said, I don't think it really conveyed why the experience of returning to his old self was supposedly so unimaginably brutal and painful that only Natsuki Subaru could endure it. Because of that, I didn't entirely understand why the female Sin Archbishop was so horrified by it, repeatedly saying how much she wanted no part of it. Obviously I understand that what Subaru went through was painful, but I still don't see why Subaru specifically was the only one capable of overcoming it.

Hearing him call her "Emilia-tan" again after so long wasn't bad, and I also liked the way the more recent Subaru entrusted everything to the original Subaru. So, with a huge amount of bonus credit, I'm giving this one a 10. Just barely, though.
review.jp:
第5話: ナツキ・スバル

"個々の記憶の集合と大元、違う時点絡みた自己といずれにしても自分というのも面白かった、大オマケ"

『Season4はずっとそうだけど、ちょっとお涙頂戴というか感動・感情に訴えかけてくる演出?展開?が多すぎる。ただ今回はこの記憶を食べられること、それを取り戻すこと、そしてそれが基本となる今までの"ナツキ・スバル"という存在に戻っていく時に、彼（彼ら）の全てが彼でなく、彼であり・・・そして彼に帰結していくということが素晴らしく描かれていたと思う。だからこそ、少しずつ他人のように思えていた他の、また大元の自信に対しても感じるものが変わっていったり、これまでの全てを取り戻した時に大元に繋がるというのも上手いな・・・面白い考えだな・・・と感じた。そしてそれぞれは個別だがきっと一貫している部分もきっとあって、感じるもの大切なものなどは変わらないのかな。自分自身でもその時じゃない自分から見たらどう見えてるかはぜんぜん違うかも知れないけど、やっぱり自分なのは変わらないのかも。そこをメインに見せていたのは良かった。ただ、彼の子に戻りの体験があまりにも壮絶でツライものでナツキ・スバルだけが耐えうる感じ・・・というのはいまいち伝わっては来なかったので、大罪司教の女があれだけ、嫌だ・・・と言っているのは良くわからなかった。そりゃあツライのはわかるけど、何故スバルだけ乗り越えられるかはわからん。久々のエミリアたん呼びは悪くはなかったし、直近スバルからの大元スバルへの託しもよかったんで、大負けにオマケして10点。ギリですけど。』

entries.title: Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia
entries.jpTitle: 天幕のジャードゥーガル

review.en:
Episode #12: The Steppe as It Always Was

"In just twelve episodes, it made me feel something almost impossibly vast out there on that same familiar grassland—and sent a shiver through me. I'm grateful."

It's difficult to put into words. I simply shuddered. That was my immediate reaction after watching Episode 12, the finale, and perhaps I don't need to say anything more or less than that. Of course, as a story, this is surely still only the beginning. And yet I thought it was a truly wonderful way to bring this part of the story to a close.

The bond between Fatima (Sitara) and Töregene may, at one point, have brought each of them close to betraying the other. But perhaps betraying the other would, at the same time, have meant betraying themselves. Those who conquer, and those who are conquered. Even after being conquered, no matter what happens to them, people go on living. But what if the life that follows isn't necessarily a bad one? And what if we look at it from the side of the conqueror? If the people you conquered go on to find happiness and live out their lives that way, then what does it actually mean to have truly conquered them...?

And within all of that, there are people like Sorqoqtani, Boraqchin, and the others—the ways they live, and the ways they die. I also found their discussion of the heavens tremendously interesting. Sitara sees herself at the center, with the stars around her divided into eight layers and revolving around her. Ögedei, meanwhile, sees people as moving while bound to the North Star—an absolute presence, almost like God. Perhaps we move intelligently and as we see fit within the particular layer to which we belong, while at the same time remaining bound to something absolute—slaves, in a sense, to fate itself.

From here, with events involving Sitara's homeland of Persia seemingly poised to set much larger changes in motion, I would absolutely love to see this series continue depicting the wider world centered around the Mongol Empire as it shifts and transforms.

With only twelve episodes to work with, I can't say there weren't moments that felt somewhat packed in, or places where I wished certain things had been explored more fully. And yet, within those limitations, could they really have shown us anything better than this? No... I don't think they could have. What they gave us was truly magnificent.

Of course, this isn't the kind of ending that leaves everything neatly resolved. Instead, against that same vast, unchanging sweep of the world and history that has always been there, it was a finale that made me want to simply sit with this series for a while longer and let its lingering presence wash over me.

To everyone involved in making this series, thank you so much for all your hard work.

Naoko Yamada... you really are something else. You're incredible. ♡
review.jp:
第12話: いつもと変わらない草原

"限られた12話だったが途方もなく大きなものをいつもの草原にて身震いとともに感じさせられた、感謝"

『うまく言えないが、ただ身震いがした。この第12話(最終回)を見た率直な感想として、それ以上でもそれ以下の言葉もいらないのかも知れない。当然物語としてはまだまだ序章に過ぎないだろう。しかし、本当に良い締めくくり方だったと思う。ファティマ(シタラ)とドレゲネとの繋がりも一度は互いに裏切ろうとしたかも知れない。しかしそれは相手を裏切ることであると同時に、自分を裏切るものであったのかも知れない。征服するものとされるもの。征服されても、どんな目にあったとしても人は生きていく。それこそその後の生活が悪いものではなかったとしたら?そして征服するものの立場でみたら?それらの征服したものがその後幸せを感じ、過ごし行きたとしたらそれこそ本当の征服なのだろう・・・。その中にある、ソルコクタニ、ボラクチン、その他の者たちのあり方となくなり方。彼らの話す天体のはなしも非常に興味深かった。自分を中心として周りの星星たちは8つのそうに分かれて回っているというシタラ。北極星＝神のような絶対的な存在に繋がれた者たちが動いているというオゴタイ・・・。それぞれの属する層において思うように賢明に動きもするし、同時に絶対的なものの、運命の?奴隷のようなものでもあるのかも知れない。今後の展開もシタラの祖国のペルシアに関わるものを発端として大きく動いていくモンゴルを中心とした世界の描きも是非見てみたい。12話という限られた話数の中で多少詰め込んだところや描き足りないのでは?と思う所がなかったわけではない。しかし、その中でこれ以上のものはあり得るか?いや・・・ないと言える素晴らしいものを見せてくれた。当然スッキリはしないが、大きな大きないつもと変わらない大局の中で、しばらくの間この作品の余韻に浸っていたいと感じさせてくれる最終回だった。制作に携わられたみなさん、本当にお疲れ様でした。山田尚子よ、あんたって人は・・・凄いね♡』

entries.synopsis:
After losing her mother and her homeland, Sitara’s despair transforms into determination with the power of knowledge. New possibilities unfold when a family of scholars takes her in, deepening her education. Meanwhile, Genghis Khan’s Mongol Empire conquers nation after nation, nearing Sitara’s new home. After the Fourth Prince of the empire takes her captive, a flame of revenge is ignited.

(Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: You and I Are Polar Opposites Season 2

review.en:
Episode #10: Feelings and Choices

"The contrast between the two couples is simply brilliant, and there's a depth to this series that comes through in the sheer beauty of Suzuki's expressions from time to time."

Honestly, I could give this a 10. The contrast between Yamada and Nishi and Tani and Suzuki—their feelings, their choices, and the actions and words that come from them—is just superb. In both couples, one person says something they don't actually want to say, something they're afraid to say, precisely because they genuinely care about the other person. And then there's the person on the other side who hears those words and accepts them. What's so interesting is that those roles are essentially reversed between the man and the woman in the two couples... though, of course, the relationships themselves and the way each pair approaches the situation are different to begin with. The delicacy with which the series presents that contrast is remarkable.

It's a road that couples who are third-year high school students, facing entrance exams and everything that comes with them, could hardly avoid.

And still, those expressions Suzuki shows every now and then... she's just so captivating. It's so well done. There's a strength and beauty to her that feels distinctly feminine, but also a weakness and timidity hidden underneath... and at the same time, there's something about her that feels expansive and embracing, as though she has the capacity to envelop someone completely. I thought the series captured all of those seemingly contradictory qualities remarkably well. And you can really feel that this is a huge part of what draws Tani to her so deeply.

And precisely because this was that kind of episode, I thought it was a great decision not to muddy its focus by cutting away to Azuma and Taira's story at all this time. They deliberately let this one stand entirely on its own.

Seriously... this was wonderful.
review.jp:
第10話: 想いと選択

"両カップルの対比が秀逸すぎる、時折見せる鈴木の表情の美しさに作品の深さを感じる"

『正直10点でもいい。山田と西、谷と鈴木の想いと選択、その行動や言葉の対比が秀逸すぎる。怖いのに本当に想っているから願ってもいないけど言う言葉、それを聞いて受けとめる側の人間が両カップルにおいて男女逆というか・・・またそもそもあり方も当然違うのだけど、その見せ方もなんとも繊細である。高校3年生・受験生のカップルが通らないはずがない道・・・。それにしても時折鈴木の見せる顔の魅力的なこと・・・。上手いなぁ・・・。女性特有の強さと美しさ、でもそこに隠された弱さと臆病さもあり…でも、その一方で何か大きく包み込むような存在でもあるというのがなんともうまくあらわされているのだと思った。きっと谷くんもそこに強く惹かれているのだろうな…というのもすごく伝わってきた。

また、こんな回だったからこそ、今回は敢えて東と平の話を一切挟んで濁さなかったのも流石だと感じた。いやいやマジで素晴らしい。 』

entries.romanized_title: Seihantai na Kimi to Boku 2nd Season
entries.synopsis: The second season of Seihantai na Kimi to Boku.

entries.title: Dara-san of Reiwa

review.en:
Episode #11: The Taboo Test of Courage

"Basically a pretty low-key episode, yet every segment works wonderfully on its own while the episode as a whole comes together just as beautifully."

So good... genuinely a little gem. I loved the first half, with the cat who has become Dara-san's servant worrying about whether its owner—the MC's homeroom teacher—will ever get married. The cat keeps exactly the same expression while we hear everything going through its mind, which makes it even better, and Dara-san's actions, the MC's actions, and every bit of dialogue between them are just perfectly judged.

And, as always, the depiction of what happened in the past after Dara-san was gone was wonderful. The series doesn't spell everything out, yet somehow knows exactly how much to show to get its message across.

Then from there we move into the test of courage involving the girl possessed by Yamatagimadara and the kids around her who have become followers of the snake, and that was fantastic too. The way it connects back to the previous segment is beautifully done. And I honestly can't tell whether Dara-san truly doesn't realize who or what she's dealing with, but her attitude toward Yamatagimadara—or rather, what's left of Yamatagimadara—is hilarious, as is Madara now having no choice but to grovel and act completely submissive around her.

What else can I say? This was just fantastic.
review.jp:
第11話: 禁断の肝試し

"基本的には地味と言える回だが、各パートがそれぞれでも良いのに全体としてのまとまりも最高"

『面白い・・・本当に珠玉。Aパートのダラさんのしもべとなった猫が飼い主である、MCの担任の結婚を案じる部分面白かったなぁ。猫の表情は一緒なのに心情を語るのもいいし、ダラさんの行動MCの行動や全ての会話も絶妙。またいつものように過去のダラさんがなくなった後の描写も素晴らしかった。すべてを語らず、しかしメッセージを伝えるうまさ。またそこからヤマタギマダラが憑いた娘とその周りでヘビの信者となった子たちとの肝試しも最高。その前のパートとの繋がりも見事だし、ダラさんが本当に気づいてないのかわからないが、ヤマタギマダラ（の残骸的存在）に対する態度と、今はヘコヘコするしかないマダラも面白かった。最高でしかないでしょう。』

entries.synopsis:
Clouds blacken the sky and sheets of rain turn the mountain forest into a treacherous maze... A landslide crushes a razor wire fence, and buries a "NO TRESPASSING" sign... Two young siblings wander into a dark world where they do not belong, and a long, horrid shadow rears up to meet them- Anyway, so that's how we met Dara-san! She might look kinda scary, but just wait until you get to know her!

"Look, I'm a god of misfortune, okay!? Aren't you kids gonna freak out about my grotesque visage!?"

(Source: Yen Press)

entries.title: Saga of Tanya the Evil II

review.en:
Episode #10: A Way to Survive

"Just as the title suggests, this is by no means a flashy episode, yet it's incredibly engaging... that sense of helpless frustration, that sheer pain of it all..."

Man... this is good. It's understated, but you can feel everyone's thoughts, their frustration, their anger... And that, in itself, is exactly what the title, "A Way Out," is getting at. They somehow manage to scrape together the best compromise they can possibly come up with, only for it to be completely outside what was expected—and ultimately miss the mark entirely. That's brutal... and fascinating to watch.
review.jp:
第10話: 活路

"まさにタイトル通り、決して派手ではない回だが、非常に楽しめる・・・このやるせなさ、つらさよ・・・"

『いやいや、、、面白い。地味だがそれぞれの想い、やるせなさ、憤り・・・。それこそタイトルの"活路"だろう。なんとかひねり出したその精一杯の妥協案が全くの想定外で見当違い・・・厳しい・・・そして面白い。』

entries.title: Iron Wok Jan!

review.en:
Episode #10: The Judges' Focus

"I do have a few doubts here and there, but the sheer intensity, fighting spirit, and entertainment value more than make up for them. This deserves a 9."

After spending so much of the previous episode showing us just how incredible Jan is, dropping the judges' score all the way down to zero on the grounds of novelty and originality may have been a little excessive—but it was certainly entertaining. Jan gets absolutely torn apart, ridiculed and criticized to no end, and even has things thrown at him, so I'm really looking forward to seeing how he picks himself back up from here.

I also couldn't help wondering whether Kiriko's dish would really become that delicious just from what she did. And as for the half-Japanese, half-French guy... would he really use gochujang? I'm pretty skeptical about that one.

Still, this was plenty entertaining!
review.jp:
第10話: 審査の焦点

"多少疑問に感じるところもあるが、それを上回る気迫・気概、そして面白さは9点に値する"

『あれだけ前回ジャンの凄さをアピールしておいて、新しさ、独創性という観点で審査員の点数0点まで下げるのは多少やりすぎにしても面白かった。トコトンバカにされ批判され物を投げられるジャン、そこから再び立ち上がるのも楽しみ。キリコの料理ってあれでそんなに美味しくなるのかな?というのもちょっと疑問だった。そして日仏ハーフの人、コチュジャンは流石に使わないんじゃない?でも十分に面白かった!』

entries.synopsis: Jan Akiyama, a cocky arrogant teenager wants to fulfill his grandfathers wish of defeating his arch nemesis Mutsuju Gobancho. When he arrives at the Gobancho restaurant he meets his granddaughter Kiriko Gobancho. Their rivalry is easily compared to Jan's and Kiriko's grandfathers, for Jan believes cooking is about competition and Kiriko believes cooking is about heart.

entries.title: Rich Girl Caretaker: I'm Secretly the Caregiver of the Most Popular Girl in This Rich Kid School
entries.jpTitle: 才女のお世話　高嶺の花だらけな名門校で、学院一のお嬢様(生活能力皆無)を陰ながらお世話することになりました

review.en:
Episode #11: The Young Lady's Showdown

"It's full of the kind of instant, effortless development you'd expect from a crappy series, but the heroines are cute, and as silly as it all is, somehow it feels like the show has actually built something up over time."

No, honestly, it's pretty awful. It shows you only the absolute bare minimum of what it really ought to show. Take how quickly and effortlessly Narika's reputation improves, for example. She does something that gets a reasonably positive reaction from one person, and then, practically the very next moment, things are already starting to turn around for her... that kind of thing.

But at this point, with this series, I'm fine with it. Mirei Tennoji and all the other heroines are cute, and I can have fun watching them. That's enough.

And the fact that my impression of the series has somehow gradually improved since entering the second half of the cour probably means that, crappy show or not, it must have built up something along the way. I have absolutely no idea what that something is, though.
review.jp:
第11話: お嬢様の対決

"クソ作品ならではのインスタントさ溢れるが、ヒロインたちが可愛い、くだらないが謎の積み重ねを感じる"

『いや、正直酷いですよ。最低限しか見せるべきことを見せないし。例えば、成香の評判が良くなるスピードとその簡単さよ。一人に何かそこそこの反応しただけで次の瞬間には改善され始める・・・とか。ただ、もう本作品においてそれはいい。天王寺美麗さんを始めヒロインがみんな可愛いし、楽しんで見れる、それでいい。クールの後半に入ってからなんとなく作品に対する印象が徐々に改善されていったのも、クソ作品ながらか積み重ねてきたものがあったのだろう。それが何かはわからないが。』

entries.romanized_title: Saijo no Osewa: Takane no Hanadarake na Meimonkou de, Gakuin Ichi no Ojou-sama (Seikatsu Nouryoku Kaimu) wo Kagenagara Osewa suru Koto ni Narimashita
entries.synopsis:
Hinako Konohana is the perfect young lady—graceful, elegant, and flawless… or so everyone thinks. Behind closed doors, she’s a total disaster who can’t handle basic chores! When ordinary student Itsuki Tomonari becomes her caretaker, he’s thrown into 24/7 damage control, maintaining her “perfect” image. It’s awkward, nonstop chaos—but it starts softening into something that feels like love…

(Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: The Cat and the Dragon

review.en:
Episode #12: The Cat and the Royal Capital's Festival

"Rather than judging this finale purely on its own, I liked it more as a culmination of the consistent themes and storytelling that ran throughout the entire cour."

If I were judging this episode entirely on its own—its execution, or simply the impression it left on me—I honestly might give it an 8. But looking at the season as a whole, I think the consistency of its storytelling deserves more credit: the many different forms of relationships between cats and humans, and the way the dragon—and perhaps the demons as well?—served to connect them. So, with a little bonus credit, I'm giving it a 9.

As a conclusion that left me feeling this really was a good series in the end, it also tied nicely back to where everything began... And ultimately, I think that was what the whole story came down to: people and cats, brought together by the dragon at the center of it all. I liked that.

Good work, O-Jingu.
review.jp:
第12話: 猫と王都の祭り

"今回の最終回単体としてというよりはクール全体として一貫したテーマや描き方への評価としてよかった"

『今回単体の出来?印象?としては正直8点かもしれないが、今シーズン通じての一貫した描き方、様々な形での猫と人、それを繋いだ竜や魔族?の描き方も良かったと言えるのかな?ということで若干オマケの9点。最終的にいい作品だったと思えるまとめとしても始まりから繋がっていたし・・・。やはり主役の竜が繋いだ人と猫というのが全てで良かった。オ・ジングお疲れ。』

entries.synopsis:
The story follows a fire-breathing, human-hating dragon raised by a mother cat in a forest. The dragon, known affectionately as "Uncle Wing," watches over the many curious cats — such as one that goes on an adventure with a human prince, and another that lives in the city and people-watches as a hobby — and gradually warms up to humans along the way.

(Source: Crunchyroll News)

entries.title: Hell Mode: The Hardcore Gamer Dominates in Another World with Garbage Balancing Season 2
entries.jpTitle: 『ヘルモード　～やり込み好きのゲーマーは廃設定の異世界で無双する～』2nd Season

review.en:
Episode #11: Unshackled/ Liberator

"With only two episodes left, it's such a shame that the series is still rushing through everything just as it has all along. I want to see so much more—including things beyond the battles—but all I can do now is see where it goes."

No, seriously, this is good. I know I've been saying the same thing over and over, but I really wish the series could have taken its time and explored everything much more thoroughly. That's the one thing I've consistently found so frustrating.

The story, character development, direction, structure, tactics, themes... they're all good. And that's exactly why the rushed pacing is such a shame. At this rate, I'm worried it'll end up being remembered as simply a very solid Narou-style isekai reincarnation series—or light-novel adaptation, I suppose—when it feels like it could have been something more.

And it really does look like they're planning to wrap this up in just two more episodes. Now the Hero is joining in too... so are we heading into battles against the demons and the Demon King? I still want the series to show us so much more, from different angles... and not just the fighting, either.

At this point, all I can do is see how it plays out.
review.jp:
第11話: 開放者

"残すところ2話、今まで同様超急ぎ足が残念でならない、戦闘以外も含めもっと見たいが見守るのみ"

『いや、面白いですよ。もうずっと同じ事を言っているけど、本当にもっとゆっくり時間をかけてじっくり描ければいい等思う。それだけがずっと残念。ストーリー、キャラクターディベロップメント、演出、構成、戦術、テーマ・・・全部いい。それだけに残念。このままだとそれなりにかなり優秀だったなろう系（ラノベ?）異世界転生作品とだけになりそうで・・・。しかもやはり後2話で終わらせようとしているのでしょうからね。勇者も参加して・・・魔人、魔人王と戦うのか?まだまだ多角的に見せてほしいなぁ・・・。戦闘以外もね。とにかく見守るしかないですよ。』

entries.title: Goodbye, Lara

review.en:
Episode #10: The Princess with a Blade

"I honestly have no idea what's going on. No matter how dramatic it's getting, I just can't get on board with it. Ironically, though, the quality keeps getting better and better."

No, seriously... I really don't get it. And when the show suddenly starts getting all dramatic and trying to build toward something huge, I just can't follow it emotionally. The witch, the king—Lara's father—her mother who was killed by humans...? Hmm... And now what was all that about Lara's "light" again?
review.jp:
第10話: 刃を持ったプリンセス

"よくわからん、盛り上がられてもついていけない。クオリティは皮肉にもますます上がってる"

『いや、マジでよくわからんすよ。そして盛り上がられてもついてけない。魔女、王様・お父さん、人間に殺されたお母さん?うーん、、、ララの光が何だって?』

entries.synopsis:
Once upon a time, a mermaid princess named Lara fell in love with a human prince. To be with him, she used a witch’s potion to become human—but the magic came at a cost: If she failed to find true love, she would vanish into sea foam forever. Now, 200 years later, Lara awakens in Lake Biwa with one final chance at life and love.

(Source: Crunchyroll)

entries.title: Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You
entries.jpTitle: スーパーの裏でヤニ吸うふたり

review.en:
Episode #10: Shining Behind the Supermarket with You

"Why the hell does Yamada suddenly decide to show up at the smoking spot and talk to Sasaki? A Christmas miracle or something? And now Obata? A supermarket workplace drama? Come on... this is boring."

What the hell was this? Christmas? Is that supposed to explain why Yamada suddenly shows up at the smoking spot—as Yamada—and starts talking to Sasaki? Some kind of Christmas miracle? And they're talking so unbelievably normally, too... Huh? No way. I just don't buy this at all.

And then there's Obata-kun, who's basically the main character of this episode. Again, out of nowhere. Huh? I really don't care...

Somehow, all of a sudden, this has turned into a story about the supermarket itself.

Ma'am, we've got an incident on our hands....
review.jp:
第10話: スーパーの裏で光る2人

"おいおい…イキナリ山田が?佐々木と?裏で?どうなってんねん、クリスマス?そして小畑?スーパー物語?いやいや、つまらん"

『は?何すかこれ?クリスマス?だから唐突に佐々木がなんと喫煙スペースで山田と会話?しかもあまりにも普通に会話してる…。は?これはないでしょう…。そしてほぼ今回の主役の小畑くん。唐突。は?どうでもいい…。突然スーパー物語になりました。ねぇさん、事件です。』

entries.romanized_title: Super no Ura de Yani Suu Futari
entries.synopsis:
The sole thing that gets the middle-aged Sasaki through his soul-sucking job is a cheerful smile from Yamada—the young woman who works at a nearby 24-hour supermarket he frequents. After every tiring day of getting berated by his boss, Sasaki stops by the store to have his spirit healed by his favorite cashier.

After a particularly grueling day, Sasaki shows up at the supermarket, only to find that Yamada's shift has already ended. Disappointed, he searches for a place to smoke when a woman from behind the store calls him over to join her. The bold and dangerously playful Tayama is quick to call out Sasaki's peculiar habit of always seeking out her coworker—even going as far as telling Yamada about Sasaki's vested interest in her.

Now, in addition to seeing his adored cashier Yamada, Sasaki also visits the store to see if his new smoking partner Tayama is around. But there is more to Tayama's mischievousness than she initially lets on. With every cigarette, an unlikely friendship begins to blossom.

[Written by MAL Rewrite]

entries.title: Ascendance of a Bookworm Season 3
entries.jpTitle: 本好きの下剋上　領主の養女

review.en:
Episode #21: Ruelle Rechallenge

"Who did this to the series? Was it the studio? Or was the source material already like this? There's barely a trace of what once made this series so great. Almost impressive, in a way."

This is just awful. I'm not finding any of this interesting anymore. And once again, they find some excuse for Rozemyne to talk directly to her biological father... Enough with the family reunions already.

Then there's all this focus on her retainers and their love lives... And apparently her aunt (?) is plotting something again. Even the issues that seem like they might actually turn into something fairly major are hard to care about, because everything leading up to them has been handled so poorly that I just can't get invested...

Rozemyne, please, say something to your big brother. What the hell happened to this series? This isn't the show I remember. Don't tell me the novels are actually like this at this point too. Does the story really get this boring? I'm seriously starting to lose interest in even watching anymore. How did we get here...?
review.jp:
第21話: リュエルに再挑戦

"誰がこうした?制作会社か?原作がそもそも?かつての輝きの欠片もない始末、ある意味お見事"

『酷すぎる、一つも面白くない。そして理由をかこつけてまた実の父と直接話している…。もう家族との再会はいいよ。そして従者?の恋愛事情ばかり…。そしてまた、叔母(?)が色々と画策しているらしい、意外と大きそうな問題なども、これまでの流れもお粗末だし、興味も持てない…。ローゼマインよ、兄上になんとか言え。一体どうなってるんだ…?こんな作品ではなかったはず。まさか、今は原作もこうなの?つまらないの?もう見る気も失せてきている。そんな馬鹿な…。』

entries.romanized_title: Honzuki no Gekokujou: Ryoushu no Youjo
entries.synopsis:
Following a disastrous encounter with a noble, Myne finally resolves to say goodbye to her family and friends in the lower city, changing her name to “Rozemyne” and beginning her new life as the adopted daughter of Ehrenfest’s archduke. However, her days as an archnoble in noble society are brutal, as she is put through rigorous etiquette and magic training on top of her duties as High Bishop and forewoman. It all proves too much for a weak little seven-year-old girl... Or it would have, had the High Priest not offered her the keys to the temple’s book room as a reward. If she could get her hands on those, she’d be able to read all sorts of precious books! Her name may have changed, but Rozemyne’s passion for books remains the same as she charges into a whole new world! The detailed setting expands as the printing industry grows in size. Here begins Part 3 of this biblio-fantasy for book lovers everywhere!

(Source: J-Novel Club)
